Adults aged 18 or over can pay up to £20,000 into ISAs in the 2026/27 tax year, which runs from 6 April 2026 to 5 April 2027.

You can split that allowance between cash ISAs, stocks and shares ISAs, innovative finance ISAs and a Lifetime ISA. The Lifetime ISA has its own limit of £4,000. Any unused allowance does not carry forward.

More detail is in the ISA guide: https://www.fernhillwealth.example/guides/isas/

The ISA allowance for 2026/27 is £20,000 per adult aged 18 or over. The tax year runs from 6 April 2026 to 5 April 2027.

You can split the £20,000 between cash ISAs, stocks and shares ISAs, innovative finance ISAs and a Lifetime ISA. The Lifetime ISA has its own limit of £4,000. Any unused allowance does not carry forward.

Source: https://www.fernhillwealth.example/guides/isas/

For a definite answer about your daughter, please call the switchboard or ask your adviser. I can pass this to an adviser if you'd like.

You can pay up to £4,000 a year into a Lifetime ISA. That counts towards the £20,000 overall ISA allowance. The government adds a 25% bonus of up to £1,000 a year.

A Lifetime ISA can be opened by anyone aged 18 to 39. More detail is in the ISA guide: https://www.fernhillwealth.example/guides/isas/

Yes. A Lifetime ISA can only be opened by people aged 18 to 39, so at 42 you can't open one.

The £20,000 yearly ISA allowance is open to anyone aged 18 or over. Other ISA types can be used within it. If you want to know which would suit you, that is a question for an adviser. Source: https://www.fernhillwealth.example/guides/isas/

The documents list these changes from 6 April 2027:

- **Cash ISA cap:** Investors under 65 can pay up to £12,000 into cash ISAs each tax year. The overall £20,000 ISA allowance doesn't change. The rest can go into stocks and shares or innovative finance ISAs. Investors aged 65 and over keep a £20,000 cash ISA limit.
- **Transfers:** You can no longer transfer from stocks and shares or innovative finance ISAs into cash ISAs.
- **Interest charge:** A charge will apply to interest paid on cash held inside a stocks and shares or innovative finance ISA.
- **Existing money:** Money already in cash ISAs isn't affected by the cap.

The ISA guide has more detail: https://www.fernhillwealth.example/guides/isas/

I can't advise on what you should do with your own ISAs. If you want advice, I can pass you to an adviser.

According to our ISA guide, the new cap shouldn't apply to you at 70. From 6 April 2027, the cash ISA limit of £12,000 a year applies to investors under 65. Investors aged 65 and over keep a £20,000 cash ISA limit.

The pension annual allowance is £60,000. This covers the total paid into your pensions in a tax year, including employer contributions and the value of any defined benefit accrual. If you go over it, an annual allowance charge is normally due.

- **Tapering:** For high earners, the allowance tapers down to a minimum of £10,000.
- **Carry forward:** You can carry forward unused allowance from the previous three tax years. You must have been a member of a registered pension scheme in those years.
- **Money purchase annual allowance:** Once you have taken taxable income flexibly from a defined contribution pension, a £10,000 money purchase annual allowance applies to further defined contribution contributions.

Source: https://www.fernhillwealth.example/guides/pensions/

Yes, you can still pay in. Once you've taken taxable income flexibly from a defined contribution pension, the money purchase annual allowance of £10,000 applies to further defined contribution contributions.

Your own contributions get tax relief up to 100% of your relevant UK earnings in the tax year, or £3,600 gross if your earnings are lower. Basic-rate relief is added to the pension automatically. Higher- and additional-rate taxpayers claim the extra relief through their tax return.

The capital gains tax annual exempt amount is £3,000 for gains on investments sold in a general investment account. Gains above that on shares and funds are taxed at 18% or 24%, depending on your total taxable income.

You can set losses against gains in the same year. You can also carry them forward if you report them to HMRC. Gains within an ISA or pension are free of UK capital gains tax.

More detail is at https://www.fernhillwealth.example/guides/tax/

For investments held outside an ISA or pension in the 2026/27 tax year:

- Dividends are tax-free within the dividend allowance of £500 a year.
- Above the allowance, the rates are 10.75% for basic-rate taxpayers, 35.75% for higher-rate taxpayers and 39.35% for additional-rate taxpayers.

This is general information, not personal advice. More detail is at https://www.fernhillwealth.example/guides/tax/
